Neurosurgery · published research

Sciatic nerve injury

Animal studies report mixed functional and histologic findings after nerve crush; human clinical evidence is absent in the exact category.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Animal studies report mixed functional and histologic findings after nerve crush; human clinical evidence is absent in the exact category.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact peripheral-nervous-system category contains 57 unique titles under sciatic nerve injury. Fifty-six are animal-tagged, and one is otherwise unclassified. No human treatment report is indexed in this exact category. Experimental papers and reviews are publications, not necessarily 56 independent injury cohorts. (de Souza et al. 2021)

Human and clinical evidence

No human clinical trial, cohort, case series, or case report was identified in the exact category. Evidence from other peripheral neuropathies should not be treated as direct evidence for traumatic sciatic nerve injury.

Animal evidence

The animal-tagged publications include 50 rat, three rabbit, and three mouse records. In a mouse sciatic-crush experiment, de Souza et al. used red PBM and reported improved sciatic functional index at a selected time point versus untreated injury controls, with no significant effect on hyperalgesia or thermography. Results from different species, injuries, and outcome measures are not directly comparable.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No stand-alone in-vitro or ex-vivo study is clearly indexed in this exact category. Any cellular measurements within animal studies remain part of those preclinical publications.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The cited mouse experiment used 660 nm visible red light, 10 J/cm², 30 mW, and 20 seconds daily for 28 days. Other studies use different wavelengths, doses, devices, and treatment durations. This protocol describes one animal experiment and cannot be assumed to be appropriate for human treatment.

Interpretation

The category provides preclinical rationale, not clinical efficacy evidence. Translation requires safety and feasibility work followed by controlled human studies with defined injury timing, severity, and nerve-function outcomes. Experimental replication should report allocation, blinding, dose, and functional measures consistently.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low for human recovery after sciatic-nerve injury Low within animal models for selected outcomes
Publications and records57 unique titles in Nervous system > PNS > Sciatic nerve injury.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The exact category contains 57 titles, 56 of them animal-tagged, with no human treatment study identified. Model protocols and outcomes vary, and publications may use related experimental models. Clinical research is needed before any treatment effect can be inferred for patients with sciatic nerve injury.
